items.name: Gulp
items.from: pressure soft bodies and the Spore cell stage. A ring of beads, springs and one pressure number.
items.hands: steer with the pointer, squeeze through gaps, spit mass to shrink and kick.
items.first: push into a gap narrower than you. Then eat five pellets and try the same gap.
items.note: The size trade-off is real with no rule written for it: a starting cell passes a 36 gap but not 26, a well-fed one needs 50. Closest of the eight to the membrane-and-cilia cell.

items.name: Wirehead
items.from: Braitenberg's vehicles, with breeding borrowed from The Bibites.
items.hands: connect two antennae to two cilia with plus and minus wires. Twelve wires in all.
items.first: cross the pellet wires and watch it turn toward food. Then press Breed.
items.note: Hand wiring scores about 27 to 38 in the test dish. Breeding reaches about 80 by finding a lopsided idle that sweeps in spirals, which is not something a person draws first. That gap is the fun.

items.name: Sprout
items.from: Cell Lab and Karl Sims' unfolding body programs.
items.hands: fill in four cell-type cards: job, when to split, what the halves become.
items.first: run Tadpole at 3x, then change one dropdown and drop a fresh germ.
items.note: Most genomes die, a few take over the dish. Tadpole filled the dish in 6 of 6 runs. Two tails on one mouth pull against each other and starve, which nobody programmed.

items.name: Cinderpit
items.hands: pour seven materials with a brush. Fewest grains wins.
items.first: flood an open cup so the pellets float out, then lay a moss fuse to the bangdust.
items.note: Fuses, floats and bombs all work from two or three rules per grain. An unplanned one: flooding the oil cup lifts the oil out over the rim, and the pellets follow. Moss overgrows anything you flood.

items.name: Mycel
items.hands: lay lure and salt. You cannot steer anything directly.
items.first: wait for the first crash, then draw a lure line from a live vein to a far pellet.
items.note: Left alone it booms and busts around 1,200 specks on average. A simple shepherding script holds about 2,100. Boom and bust is strong and may want softening.

items.name: Bloomfield
items.hands: paint feed, walls and spores into a living stain.
items.first: draw one thin feed line to the nearest pellet and watch spots divide along it.
items.note: On quiet ground spots hold still forever. A feed line makes them bud along it one after another. It is slow and meditative, the least game-like of the set.

items.name: Gaitkeeper
items.from: Sodarace and Karl Sims' evolved creatures.
items.hands: place joints, bones and muscles. Breeding picks the muscle rhythm.
items.first: press Let it go, then Breed a gait, on the same body.
items.note: Untrained bodies move about 15. Bred ones reach 400 to 500 in half a second of breeding. Small body edits change the gait completely.

items.name: Motley
items.hands: edit a five by five table of likes and dislikes, live.
items.first: start from Blank, then give one colour +1 toward pale.
items.note: Random tables crack between 0 and 176 pellets in 25 seconds, so the table matters a lot. When every colour could smell pellets the game was trivial, so now only pale can.

next.name: Wired cell
next.what: Gulp's soft body with Wirehead's wiring. Sensors and cilia sit on the membrane and you connect them, so steering comes from the body instead of the pointer.
next.params: 22 beads, 4 sensor sites, 4 cilia sites, wires at -1/0/+1, 40 s rounds, breed 15 generations of 20

next.name: Cell in the pit
next.what: Gulp's cell swimming inside Cinderpit's grain world, where water, oil, moss and bangdust are both hazard and tool.
next.params: 180 x 112 grains, 20 bead cell, 6 chambers, cell can carry and drop one material

next.name: Grown machines
next.what: Sprout's cards driving the parts sandbox from the other thread, so slingshots and whips are grown from a germ instead of placed by hand.
next.params: 4 types x 6 settings, bond kinds rod/spring/rope, dish cap 160

next.name: Bigger brains
next.what: Wirehead with two inner neurons, a touch sense and a hunger sense, to see where hand wiring stops being readable.
next.params: 8 senses, 2 inner, 2 cilia, breed 30 generations of 40, 3 dishes

next.name: Living pond
next.what: Wirehead swimmers that breed in the dish as they eat, with you as gardener moving pellets and poison.
next.params: start 40 swimmers, cap 120, mutation 0.2 per wire, split at energy 1.5

next.name: Species hunt
next.what: A search over Motley tables for bodies that travel, heal and feed, to give a shelf of found species to start from.
next.params: 2,000 tables, 5 colours, half-step values, 35 s each, about 25 minutes on four threads

notBuilt: Lenia and neural cellular automata (smooth creatures that regrow when cut) and Avida (programs that evolve to compute) were on the list. Both are harder to put hands on, so they come after a first reaction to these eight.
